goal: Close the auditors' finding that any Pod can reach Meridian Freight's payments-api by building default-deny plus one selective allow - and then determine honestly whether this cluster's CNI enforces any of it.
produces: A default-deny-all NetworkPolicy (podSelector {}, Ingress and Egress) plus the DNS egress rule that default-deny otherwise breaks
A matched ingress/egress pair admitting only role=frontend to app=payments-api on the POD port 8080, diffed against data/traffic-matrix.csv
A recorded enforcement determination: the CNI DaemonSet inventory and a live probe whose result is reported rather than assumed
concepts: kind's default CNI kindnet stores NetworkPolicies and enforces none - the API is universal, enforcement is the CNI's job
There is no deny rule: a Pod becomes deny-by-default the moment any policy selects it, and allows are the union of all matching rules
NetworkPolicy ports are Pod ports, evaluated below the Service abstraction after kube-proxy's DNAT
namespaceSelector and podSelector in one peer item are ANDed; split across two items they are ORed
